messages.subject: Great resource for grad students and early career researchers
messages.subject_clean: Great resource for grad students and early career researchers
messages.body_plain:
Dear Colleagues,

Ran across this FREE excellent academic platform called figbox I would like to share with everyone. Click here: https://figbox.co/.

According to their FAQs  fIgbox allow early career researchers and junior scholars the ability support each other through the exchange of feedback, academic content, etc in the following categories:
General career advice
Thesis selection/ literature review
Submission/publication advice
Postdocs applying for junior professorship positions
Quantitively and qualitative analyses
Methodological approach and design
Feedback on working scholarship/grant
Feedback on working paper
Feedback on working thesis
Replying to referee reviews from journal
Handling academic conflicts
Transitioning from academia into workplace
In exchange early career researchers:
Increase their mentorship/ peer-review experience
Receive verified mentorship certificates in support of CV and career
Get mentorship advice (e.g. grant proposal) from other early career researchers.
Receive optional lunch money from mentees they support
Best Regards,
Casey, M
Masters Student, University of Chicago

messages.subject: Updated Hierarchical Modeling in Ecology landing page: www.hierarchicalmodels.com
messages.subject_clean: Updated Hierarchical Modeling in Ecology landing page: www.hierarchicalmodels.com
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

we have just updated the Hierarchical Modeling landing page which is meant to give a concise and informative overview of our Hierarchical Modeling in Ecology projects. Please see here: www.hierarchicalmodels.com <http://www.hierarchicalmodels.com>.

Major new things are:
Fully updated links for the new book on Integrated Population Models (IPMs; due just before Christmas ... 🙂 ....). There are links to two Github pages that contain all the code in the book and more (big thanks to Mike Meredith for that).
We have a new section called "Web tutorials". Right now it features Mike Meredith's superbly useful introduction to JAGS for wildlife researchers; check it out soon.
Finally, we have added a section entitled "Hierarchical models in action....", where you can download (for FREE !) an English pdf of the latest Swiss Breeding Bird Atlas which (we hope) is a nice advertisement for binomial N-mixture and site-occupancy models applied in a large-scale SDM project.
One major thing still missing is that we must soon update/create short websites for the two AHM books .... first things on our list towards the end of this year.

*** Many thanks to Jim Hines from Patuxent for maintaining the website ***

Best regards  --- Marc and colleagues

messages.subject: PhD position in avian ecology
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

Please help me spread the word about the position described below.

Thanks,
Richard

PhD position in avian ecology

https://chandlerlab.uga.edu/opportunities/

A PhD position is available in the Chandler Lab at the University of Georgia to study avian reproductive performance and nest predation over climate gradients in the southern Appalachian Mountains. The PhD student will design and execute field experiments, develop models of spatio-temporal predator-prey dynamics, and forecast the effects of climate change on avian productivity. Study species include Canada Warbler, Black-throated Blue Warbler, Veery, and several others with trailing-edge populations in western North Carolina. Eight years of data on distribution and demography are available from the study area. Applicants should have an MS degree in wildlife ecology or a related field, strong quantitative skills, and passerine field experience. The anticipated start date is August 2022. Tuition will be waived and an assistantship of approximately $25,000/yr for four years will be provided. Send a single PDF including a cover letter, CV, and contact information for three references to Richard Chandler (rcha...@warnell.uga.edu) by November 10, 2021.
